Jordan Lee Crawford was born on October 23, 1988.
Jordan Lee Crawford is an American professional basketball player.
Jordan Lee Crawford plays for the Sichuan Blue Whales of the Chinese Basketball Association (CBA).
Jordan Lee Crawford played college basketball for Indiana University and Xavier University.
Jordan Lee Crawford's brother is Joe Crawford.
Joe Crawford has also played in the NBA.
Jordan Lee Crawford was born to Joseph Sr. and Sylvia Crawford in Detroit, Michigan.
In high school, Jordan Lee Crawford suffered an ankle injury which forced him to miss his senior year of basketball.
Jordan Lee Crawford attended Communication and Media Arts High School in Detroit.
Jordan Lee Crawford attended Hargrave Military Academy in Chatham, Virginia.
Jordan Lee Crawford signed a National Letter of Intent to play at Indiana University and enrolled in 2007.
In the 2007–2008 season, Jordan Lee Crawford played 30 games as a freshman at Indiana starting eight times.
In the 2007–2008 season, Jordan Lee Crawford finished seventh among Big Ten Conference freshmen in scoring with 9.7 points per game.
In the 2007–2008 season, Jordan Lee Crawford helped Indiana finish 25–8 overall and 14–4 in the Big Ten.
In the 2007–2008 season, Jordan Lee Crawford advanced to the NCAA tournament with Indiana.
In the 2007–2008 season, Jordan Lee Crawford scored in double figures 15 times as a freshman.
In the 2007–2008 season, Jordan Lee Crawford had a career high 21 points in Indiana's win at Northwestern on February 23, 2008.
In the 2007–2008 season, Jordan Lee Crawford went for 6-for-7 overall and 4-for-5 behind the three-point line while handing out all five of his assists against Northwestern.
In the 2007–2008 season, Jordan Lee Crawford made all five of his free throw attempts at the free throw line against Northwestern.
Indiana recorded a 13–2 record when Jordan Lee Crawford scored in double figures during the 2007–2008 season.
After the Kelvin Sampson controversy, Jordan Lee Crawford transferred to Xavier University in 2008.
Xavier was one of only two nonconference regular season losses for Indiana University in the 2007–2008 season when Jordan Lee Crawford was at Indiana University.
Due to NCAA rules, Jordan Lee Crawford had to sit out the 2008–2009 season but could practice with Xavier.
In the summer of 2009, rumors circulated that a college player dunked on LeBron James in a pickup game at a mini-camp cosponsored by James and Nike.
Jordan Lee Crawford was rumored to have made the feat at the LeBron James Skills Academy.
Footage leaked out about a week later on YouTube.
In the 2009–2010 season, Jordan Lee Crawford led Xavier and the Atlantic 10 in scoring with 20.5 points per game.
Jordan Lee Crawford had .462 FG% during the 2009–2010 season at Xavier.
Jordan Lee Crawford scored in double figures in 31 straight games and 34 of XU's 35 games during the 2009–2010 season.
In the 2009–2010 season, Jordan Lee Crawford scored 20+ points in 20 games for the Musketeers.
Jordan Lee Crawford was named to the First Team All-Atlantic 10 in the 2009–2010 season.
Xavier won its fourth straight A-10 title and earned a 6-seed in the NCAA tournament during the 2009–2010 season.
Jordan Lee Crawford led the Musketeers past the 3-seed Pittsburgh Panthers to their third straight Sweet Sixteen, one of only two teams to accomplish this during '08–'10.
Xavier lost to the 2-seed Kansas State Wildcats in the West Regional semifinal during the 2009–2010 season.
Jordan Lee Crawford scored a career high 32 points in the double overtime thriller against Kansas State, including a deep three-pointer sending the game to the second overtime.
Jordan Lee Crawford earned a spot on the five-member NCAA Tournament All-West Region Team after averaging 29.0 points per game in the three appearances during the 2009–2010 season.
Jordan Lee Crawford scored more points (718) for a sophomore than any other in Xavier's history during the 2009–2010 season.
Jordan Lee Crawford finished fourth in the Musketeer's single-season scoring history during the 2009–2010 season.
Jordan Lee Crawford was selected by the New Jersey Nets with the 27th overall pick in the 2010 NBA draft.
Due to his play style, Jordan Lee Crawford was nicknamed "Sizzle".
Jordan Lee Crawford's rights were later traded to the Atlanta Hawks and he joined the team for the 2010 NBA Summer League.
On February 23, 2011, Jordan Lee Crawford was traded to the Washington Wizards along with Maurice Evans and Mike Bibby.
On March 8, 2011, Jordan Lee Crawford scored a then-career high 22 points against the Milwaukee Bucks.
On March 15, 2011, Jordan Lee Crawford passed his previous career high by scoring 27 points in a loss to the Chicago Bulls.
On March 30, 2011, Jordan Lee Crawford set a new career high by scoring 39 points in a loss to the Miami Heat.
On April 1, 2011, Jordan Lee Crawford recorded his first triple-double of his professional career with 21 points, 11 assists, and 10 rebounds against the Cleveland Cavaliers.
Jordan Lee Crawford was the second Wizards rookie that season to record a triple double after John Wall.
In the 2012–13 season, Jordan Lee Crawford became the starting point guard of the team when John Wall missed time due to injury.
On November 29, 2013, Jordan Lee Crawford recorded his third triple-double with 11 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in a 103–86 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On December 9, 2013, Jordan Lee Crawford was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week after averaging 23.3 points, 6.1 assists, and 3 rebounds on 61 percent shooting during the week.
On February 21, 2013, Jordan Lee Crawford was traded to the Boston Celtics for Leandro Barbosa and Jason Collins.
In his debut with the Celtics, Jordan Lee Crawford came off the bench to record 2 assists, 3 rebounds, and 10 points, shooting 4 for 9 from the field.
Due to Rajon Rondo's injury, Jordan Lee Crawford became the starting point guard of the team at the beginning of the 2013–14 season.
On November 29, 2013, Jordan Lee Crawford recorded his third triple-double with 11 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in a 103–86 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On January 15, 2014, a three-team trade was completed involving the Boston Celtics, the Golden State Warriors, and the Miami Heat.

The Celtics sent Jordan Lee Crawford and MarShon Brooks to the Warriors in exchange for Joel Anthony, a protected future draft pick Philadelphia sent to Miami in an earlier trade, and a 2016 second-round draft pick from the Heat.
On April 16, 2014, Jordan Lee Crawford scored a career high 41 points in a 116–112 win over the Denver Nuggets in the final regular season game of the season.
On September 18, 2014, Jordan Lee Crawford signed a one-year deal with the Xinjiang Flying Tigers of the Chinese Basketball Association.
Jordan Lee Crawford left Xinjiang in November 2014 after appearing in just five games.
On March 10, 2015, Jordan Lee Crawford was acquired by the Fort Wayne Mad Ants of the NBA Development League.
In 14 games for the Mad Ants, Jordan Lee Crawford averaged 24.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, 4.9 assists and 2.2 steals per game.
In July 2015, Jordan Lee Crawford joined the Dallas Mavericks for the 2015 NBA Summer League.
On September 28, 2015, Jordan Lee Crawford signed with the Chicago Bulls.
On October 22, 2015, Jordan Lee Crawford was waived by the Chicago Bulls after appearing in five preseason games.
On November 19, 2015, Jordan Lee Crawford returned to China and signed with Tianjin Ronggang.
On January 8, 2016, Jordan Lee Crawford scored 72 of the team's 104 points in a loss to the Sichuan Blue Whales.
Jordan Lee Crawford shot 25-of-52 from the field, including 4-of-12 from three-point range, and was 18-of-20 from the free throw line during that game.
On October 30, 2016, Jordan Lee Crawford was acquired by the Grand Rapids Drive of the NBA Development League.
On March 6, 2017, Jordan Lee Crawford signed a 10-day contract with the New Orleans Pelicans.
That night, Jordan Lee Crawford scored 19 points against the Utah Jazz in his first NBA appearance since April 16, 2014.
On March 16, 2017, Jordan Lee Crawford signed with the Pelicans for the remainder of the 2016–17 season.
Three days later, on March 19, 2017, Jordan Lee Crawford had a season-high 22 points in 21 minutes in a 123–109 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves.
On October 22, 2017, Jordan Lee Crawford was waived by the Pelicans after appearing in the team's first two games of the 2017–18 season.
On April 5, 2018, Jordan Lee Crawford was signed for the remainder of the season by the Pelicans.
On November 19, 2018, Jordan Lee Crawford signed a one-month contract with Alba Berlin.
Two days later, on November 21, 2018, Jordan Lee Crawford's contract with Alba Berlin was rescinded after he didn't pass the physicals.
On January 8, 2019, Jordan Lee Crawford signed with the Israeli team Ironi Nahariya for the remainder of the season.

On January 27, 2019, Jordan Lee Crawford recorded 21 points in his third game with Ironi Nahariya, shooting 4-for-9 from three-point range, along with two rebounds and five assists, leading Ironi Nahariya to a 86–80 win over Hapoel Jerusalem.
On February 13, 2019, Jordan Lee Crawford parted ways with Ironi Nahariya after appearing in five games.
On February 25, 2020, Jordan Lee Crawford signed with Brose Bamberg of the German Basketball Bundesliga (BBL).
On July 3, 2020, Jordan Lee Crawford signed with Lokomotiv Kuban of the VTB United League.
On February 24, 2021, Jordan Lee Crawford signed with Galatasaray of the Turkish Basketball Super League (BSL).
On December 30, 2021, Jordan Lee Crawford signed with the Long Island Nets of the NBA G League.
In eight games for the Long Island Nets, Jordan Lee Crawford averaged 13.4 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game.
Jordan Lee Crawford was waived on January 31, 2022.
On March 11, 2022, Jordan Lee Crawford was reacquired by the Long Island Nets.
On April 7, 2022, Jordan Lee Crawford signed with Gigantes de Carolina from Puerto Rico.
